newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian senator calls for 1997 budget approval.
newsitem.headline: Russian senator calls for 1997 budget approval.

text.p: The head of the budget committee of Russia's Federation Council upper house of parliament urged the chamber on Wednesday to approve the 1997 budget but said the government should also take account of the house's proposals.

"If we return the budget to the lower chamber we will not gain much. Taking into account the government's latest suggestions, I recommend that the budget should be approved," Konstantin Titov told the house in the presence of the cabinet.
But he called on the government to pay off fully social benefit arrears from last year, as proposed by the Federation Council.

Earlier Finance Minister Alexander Livshits urged the deputies to approve the budget, saying the draft was realistic. He said the budget would help keep inflation from rising, reduce yields on government securities and bring about economic growth.
The draft envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, by Russian calculations, on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles and expenditure of 529.8 trillion roubles.

The State Duma lower house of parliament approved the draft at a fourth final reading on January 24. It now passes to the Federation Council for consideration. It also requires approval by Yeltsin before becoming law.
